messages:
Maya: Quick design check: we need a clean lifecycle for service principals (create, rotate, retire) and a clear enforcement path (monitor -> soft-enforce -> hard-enforce) for migrating API-key users to principal-based RBAC. Thoughts?
Ethan: +1. concretely: how are principals created? automated per-key? manual only?
Maya: Prefer automated creation during a discovery pass, but flagged as 'proposed' until owner approves. That avoids mass manual work.
Ravi: We should define states: proposed, active, suspended, retired. Each state has allowed operations and retention.
Sofia: Enforcement modes matter. In monitor mode we only emit metrics and console suggestions. In soft-enforce we accept both old key and principal but count principal as preferred. In hard-enforce we reject old keys. Timeline must be configurable per org.
Maya: Agree. Example sequence for migration: 1) discovery run -> list keys 2) propose principals 3) owners review in Console 4) enable soft-enforce for product 5) cutover window -> hard-enforce 6) retire keys.
Ethan: For discovery heuristics we can reuse metadata heuristics: key_name, creator, scopes, last_seen. Also inspect common call patterns (endpoints touched) to build suggested role templates.
Ravi: Role templates idea: represent common permission bundles (svc.ingest, svc.query, svc.admin). Templates map to lower-level permissions. Bindings attach principals to templates at org/project scope.
Sofia: Need to handle third-party webhooks and CI systems which can't do mTLS. For those we allow long-lived principal tokens with strict IP and rate limits, and require rotation every X days.
Maya: Audit needs: every principal creation/approval/rotation must write an audit record including source (discovery/manual), key fingerprint (sha256), approver id, and timestamp.
Ethan: What about cross-project delegation? e.g., a billing service that reads multiple projects. Option A: grant org-level role; Option B: create a principal with multiple project bindings. Prefer B for least privilege but UI must support multi-binding easily.
Ravi: Data model sketch: principal {id: "svc-<uuid>", owners: [user-id], bindings: [binding-id], state: "proposed"}. binding {id, principal_id, role_template, scope_type: org|project, scope_id}. Keep simple.
Sofia: Ops: for hosted we will manage tokens and rotation. For Dedicated/Private customers, provide a management API and an optional agent that performs rotation locally and syncs state.
Maya: Revocation flow: mark principal suspended -> invalidate active tokens -> record audit. Need propagation to edge caches. Add pub/sub invalidation channel and short token TTL to limit blast radius.
Ethan: Token design: short-lived JWTs for runtime (exp 30s-2m) minted by control plane; long-lived bootstrap tokens for CI (rotate every 30 days) exchanged for short-lived runtime tokens via token-exchange endpoint.
Ravi: Console UX: endpoints: show 'migration health' per product, list proposed principals, provide approve/reject and bulk-approve via CSV. Also exportable audit log link.
Sofia: API compatibility: add header X-Auth-Principal: svc-<id> when principal used, and X-Legacy-Key: key-id-hash while in soft-enforce. We should avoid leaking full key.
Maya: Security: require MFA for principal approval actions for org-admins. Also threshold for auto-approve: if key created by same owner and last_used < 90 days, auto-propose but still require explicit opt-in for auto-bind.
Ethan: Metrics we'll track: principal_proposed, principal_approved, principal_rejected, mapping_confidence_score (0-100), legacy_key_hits, token_issuance_latency_p95.
Ravi: Edge case: ephemeral batch jobs that spawn huge parallelism. We must ensure token issuance doesn't become bottleneck. Suggest caching exchanged tokens local to job runners for TTL and bulk-exchange API.
Sofia: Compliance: retention of audit events 7 years for enterprise customers on request. Built-in policy should keep 1 year by default.
Maya: Implementation plan: week1 spike for discovery + proposed principal model, week2 console UI + audit plumbing, week3 proxy/token-exchange and soft-enforce, week4 pilot with 1 product team, week6 roll to org.
security-bot: New checklist created: https://redwood.internal/security/principal-migration-checklist (owners assigned)
Ethan: I'll own the discovery spike and produce CSV of candidates.
Ravi: I'll draft the minimal JSON schema for principal and binding and post here.
Sofia: I'll draft the enforcement mode flags and retention SLA language for the RFC.
Maya: Thanks. We'll reconvene Friday to review spike results and pick pilot team.
